config.title: Network Delay Time

intro.title: Network Delay Time
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll implement a solution to calculate the minimum time for a signal to reach all nodes in a network using Dijkstra's algorithm. You'll learn how to model network connections as a weighted graph and find the shortest path from a starting node to all other nodes. The implementation will involve using JavaScript arrays, objects, and priority queues to efficiently process node distances. By completing this exercise, you'll understand fundamental graph traversal concepts and how to apply them to real-world network lessons.
intro.usecase: The Network Delay Time algorithm is essential for optimizing communication networks in real-world applications like GPS navigation systems, where it calculates the minimum time for traffic updates to propagate through road networks. Cloud service providers use this algorithm to determine the maximum latency for data packets traveling between servers in distributed systems, ensuring service level agreements are met. In multiplayer online games, it helps identify the slowest connection in player networks to synchronize game states effectively. Network administrators apply this to monitor and troubleshoot latency issues in enterprise IT infrastructure dashboards.

objectives: Construct a graph data structure to represent network nodes and weighted edges
Initialize a distance array to track minimum travel times from the source node
Implement Dijkstra's algorithm to find shortest paths in a weighted graph
Manipulate a priority queue to efficiently select the next node to process
Update node distances when a shorter path through a neighbor is discovered
Configure the algorithm to handle edge cases like unreachable nodes
Integrate all components to calculate the maximum delay time across the network
